description:
Six days before Thanksgiving, Grandma Bev posts two coffee cups with a heart, a hand on a steering wheel and a blurry elbow. Her granddaughter Nia goes full detective, the family group chat panics, and the dog knows more than he is saying.

#cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #thanksgiving
tiktok_caption: grandma posted two coffee cups and a heart. six days before thanksgiving 👀☕ #cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #thanksgiving

lines.text: Grandma just posted a picture of two coffee cups. Two. With a heart.
Good morning, sweetheart. I do not know what you are talking about.
You put a heart on a cup, Grandma. You have never put a heart on anything. Not even me.
I am Sergeant. I am the dog. I was there. It was a very nice cup.
I am seventy four. I am allowed to drink coffee across from somebody.
Across from who?
Somebody.
Okay. Detective mode. Picture number two. A hand on a steering wheel.
That is a man's hand. That hand has a watch. Grandpa never wore a watch.
Grandpa said time was a suggestion. He was late to our wedding.
The hand smells like peppermint and good decisions.
Whose car is that, Grandma? Your car has a fuzzy pink wheel cover.
Maybe I changed. People change. Wheel covers change.
You have had that wheel cover since nineteen ninety eight. It has seen things.
It has. Mostly the drive thru.
Picture number three. A blurry elbow. At the bowling alley. Wearing a sweater.
That could be anybody's elbow.
It has a patch on it, Grandma. Only two kinds of people have elbow patches. Professors and men who say 'well actually'.
He does not say 'well actually'. He says 'interesting'.
Ha! He! You said he!
I said he like a pronoun. Like a normal person.
Grandma. Thanksgiving is in six days. Is the elbow coming to Thanksgiving?
The elbow will be seated by the window. The elbow likes natural light.
I am texting the family group chat.
Do not text the group chat. Your uncle Ray types with one finger. It takes him a week to panic.
Too late. Uncle Ray says, quote, who is the elbow, question mark, question mark, little turkey.
He sends the little turkey to everybody. He sent it to his dentist. The dentist sent one back.
Aunt Denise replied with a picture of a lawyer.
Mom wants to know if he has a pension.
He has a pension, a boat and a very good knee. One knee. The other knee is fine.
A boat? Grandma, you get seasick in the bathtub.
That is why I sit at the front of the bath.
Why the mystery? Why not just post his face like a normal grandma?
Because that is how you do it, baby. You hide them for a while. Two cups. A hand. An elbow.
I learned it from somebody.
From who?
She learned it from you.
Eight months, Nia. Eight months of two cups on your page. A hand on your steering wheel.
That is my friend's hand.
Your friend has a watch. Your friend smells like peppermint.
How do you know what my friend smells like?
Because I have been having coffee with your friend every Tuesday since August.
What?
I found the coffee shop from the cups. Same chipped saucer. I sat down at the next table and said, interesting.
Grandma, you staked out my boyfriend?
She brought me. I was the undercover dog.
He does the crossword in pen. He drove me to bowling when my wheel cover fell off. He is a good boy.
I am the good boy. He is a good man.
So the hand, the elbow, the boat...
The boat is his uncle's. It is a canoe. I said boat to scare your mother.
Why would you soft post my boyfriend before I did?
Because you were never going to bring him. And I am seventy four. I do not buy green bananas.
Hi. Sorry. Is this a bad time? Bev said to come in at the elbow part.
Darius!
Peppermint. Called it.
I brought a pie. Bev said if I brought a pie I could sit by the window.
Natural light. Very important for an elbow.
I cannot believe my grandma introduced my boyfriend to my family before I did.
Your uncle Ray just texted me a little turkey.
That is his highest honor. Even the dentist only got one.
Fine. Grandma, take a picture of us. Our faces. No elbows.
Absolutely not. Hold up two cups and look at the window.
Somebody post the dog. I am ready to be launched.
